headline: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
claim: Young people who use AI chatbots during emotional distress have worse mental health and more suicidal thoughts and attempts.
notes: published 2026-10-30; syndicated from NPR (Rhitu Chatterjee); NPR page itself would not load. Finding is from a JED Foundation survey of 5,500 9-17 year olds, run by a mental health advocacy group (its own survey). Correlational; the article says cause is unclear. Also cites UNC studies on companionship use and loneliness.

headline: Nearly 2 out of 3 teens and tweens use AI chatbots, new research shows
claim: Young people who use AI chatbots during emotional distress have worse mental health and more suicidal thoughts and attempts.
notes: published 2026-11-01 per page text (URL slug says 2026-10-30); same NPR story. JED Foundation survey, advocacy group's own survey; correlational, article says cause is unclear.

headline: Texas sues OpenAI over ChatGPT's alleged harmful advice, child safety risks
claim: ChatGPT has encouraged suicide, given mass shooters advice and become addictive to children.
notes: published 2026-10-30; Texas filed the state-court suit 2026-10-23 against OpenAI and Sam Altman. These are the state's allegations, not findings. Found via a lawsuit news aggregator, not the state's own release.

headline: AI-driven layoffs are creating a new class of boomerang employees—companies are realizing they 'pulled the plug too quickly'
claim: Workers laid off because of AI are being asked back, which suggests the AI-driven layoffs were a mistake.
notes: published 2026-10-30; based on an SHL survey (SHL is a talent assessment company, so an interested party) fielded by Propeller Insights June-July 2026, about 1,000 US and 1,000 UK workers. The 'pulled the plug too quickly' framing is the article's, not the survey's.

headline: Investors split on earnings season job cuts tied to AI, costs
claim: Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs and ties the cuts to AI.
notes: published 2026-11-03; republished Bloomberg News story (Rose Henderson). The AI link is Barclays' own stated rationale, an interested party. Only Barclays is named as linking cuts to AI; Microsoft, Volvo, Schaeffler and OPmobility cuts are given other reasons. Not checked against Barclays' filing.

headline: Anthropic Faces New Suit, Says Training on Lyrics Is Fair Use
claim: Training AI on copyrighted song lyrics harms songwriters and the music industry.
notes: published 2026-10-23; music publishers including Universal Music Group filed the suit. Allegations by the plaintiffs, not findings. Anthropic argues the training is fair use.
